thread:
Anika Patel: Evening oncall here — quick async standup from my shift. TL;DR: 2 active issues (embedding evictions + a sporadic kvproxy error). Did: triaged alerts, bumped embed cache size for affected pool, created short watchdog that restarts the exporter on OOM. Blockers: still seeing occasional kvproxy 502s when traffic spikes; not reproducible locally. Today: leave notes for next shift, follow up on kvproxy tracing, and watch CPU on kvcache nodes.
Liam O'Connor: Thanks — noted. For kvproxy 502s did you see any correlation with autoscaler churn? Last night we got a scale-in shortly before the spikes. I can add a temporary cluster autoscaler buffer for the next 2 hours if you want.
Anika Patel: Good call — I saw a scale-in ~2:07a UTC and a small bump in 95th latency at 2:10a. Please add a +2 buffer for the cluster group handling inference-embeds. That should reduce the cold-starts. :thumbsup:
Sofia Ramirez: Re: embedding evictions — what was the command you used to increase the pool? Want to make the change durable in k8s config.
Anika Patel: Ran this one-off while debugging:
```
kubectl patch deployment kvcache-pool-eu-west -n inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"24Gi"}]'
```
I also pushed a tiny PR to orchestration that updates pool defaults: https://git.internal/redwood/orch/pull/482 (small change, needs review + merge). Marked it w/ priority so it can be merged by oncall if safe.
Matt Huang: I'll take the PR and do a quick safety check. If it's good I can merge and roll it out. Also I'll add a brief note to the runbook about the temp exporter restart script you mentioned.
incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-17: "kvcache eviction spike causing elevated embed latencies" — Severity: S2 — Status: investigating — Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-17
Liam O'Connor: Minor repro details: curl against /v1/embeds during peak returns 502 intermittently. I attached a small capture to the incident. I'm going to enable trace-level logs on kvproxy for 15 minutes to get more context.
Anika Patel: Sounds good. Next steps for next shift:
- Watch INC-2026-17 and update status (Sofia/Matt) if mitigation holds
- Keep autoscaler buffer +2 for the group until 06:00 UTC
- If kvproxy 502s persist, flip kvproxy to the fallback route (route: embed-fallback) — I left the toggle in configstore under /feature/ops/kv-fallback
- Merge PR 482 and monitor kvcache memory usage
Sofia Ramirez: I'll own monitoring for next shift. I'll check logs, confirm the exporter restarts are stable, and post an update in the incident thread. If anything urgent comes up ping me directly @sofia.
Matt Huang: Merging PR 482 in 10m after a quick smoke test. I'll notify here when done. Can someone confirm that load-tests are disabled for eu-west while we have this rolling? Don't want noisy churn.
Anika Patel: I turned off the synthetic load tests earlier (job: synthetic-embed-heat) — confirmed off. Also left a quick snippet to roll back if memory bump causes evictions:
```
kubectl patch deployment kvcache-pool-eu-west -n inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"16Gi"}]'
```
Liam O'Connor: I'll keep traces on for another 10m and drop results into the incident. If I see a clear pattern, I'll propose a follow-up fix (likely connection pooling tweak).
Anika Patel: Thanks team. If no major regressions by 06:00 UTC I plan to close the active mitigation and hand off long-term follow-ups to platform backlog. Leaving the incident in investigating until kvcache metrics stabilize. :white_check_mark:
Matt Huang: PR merged, rolling update started. Will post status when pods are ready.
Sofia Ramirez: Watching pods. 3/3 ready on kvcache-pool-eu-west replicas. No new evictions in the last 5m. Posting to INC-2026-17: "mitigation applied, monitoring".
Anika Patel: Great — handing off. Oncall notes in runbook under /ops/oncall/shift-notes/2026-03-17-eve. Ping if anything spikes. — Anika
